findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:0 evidence cites the 'sanity-bound' case at packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:442-448 as proof that the retained sanity bound 'is exercised rather than silently absent,' but that case only asserts TRANSCRIPT.length > 200_000 and that the digest matches /^story_advance\/[0-9a-f]{12}$/ -- a well-formed-digest check that passes identically whether or not the .slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS) bound exists in convergence-breaker.ts:483-485. Verified empirically: removed the .slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS) call from convergence-breaker.ts, rebuilt, and ran this exact assertion pair in isolation against the bound-removed build -- it still PASSED. The bound-removed build IS caught, but by a different case: 'must-still-collapse beyond-sanity-bound' (smoke.ts:337-341, MUST_COLLAPSE lane), which is the evidence cited for the separate intent CHK-001:edge:1, not for edge:0. So CHK-001:edge:0 has no valid evidence of its own claimed property; that property is established elsewhere under a different intentRef. This is an evidence note that restates the intent rather than an assertion that proves it. Net risk is low (the bound is genuinely tested by edge:1), but the edge:0 evidence record itself does not cover what it claims.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 — the narrowed digit-rule regex `(?<![\w-])\d+(?![\w-])` only treats a digit run as identifier-attached when preceded/followed by a word char or ASCII hyphen; a `.` does not protect. Verified empirically: normalize("requires lattice-cli v0.3.229 or newer") and normalize("requires lattice-cli v0.3.230 or newer") both reduce to "requires lattice-cli v0.#.# or newer" (identical digest). Any rejection reason embedding a dotted version/semver string (a realistic shape given version-bump.ts already formats messages like "expected X.Y.Z") collapses two substantively different failures into one gate-failure key -- exactly the C4 over-collapse class this story exists to fix, for a token shape CHK-003/CHK-004 never exercises. gateFailureDigest is exported general-purpose, not scoped to the one current call site.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 — the digit-rule lookbehind/lookahead `(?<![\w-])...(?![\w-])` excludes a preceding/following ASCII hyphen unconditionally, which also matches a minus sign, so a negative number is treated as identifier-attached and survives instead of collapsing. Verified: normalize("retry budget -5 remaining") vs normalize("retry budget -19 remaining") do NOT collapse (stay distinct), unlike the documented free-standing-counter behavior in the surrounding comment (attempt 41, 3>=2, 0/4 lanes all correctly collapse). This under-collapses an incidental numeric difference, i.e. it is a live instance of the exact risk plan.md #4 calls out as the change's central danger ("the change makes the breaker fire less often ... a stuck agent [could] regain an unbounded retry loop"), for a token shape (negative numbers) the CHK-004 must-still-collapse lane never tests.
